about: BYJU'S is a Bengaluru-based Indian education technology company, founded in 2011 by Byju Raveendran, known for its learning app with video lessons, tutoring and test prep aimed at school students, and for acquiring Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Great Learning and Epic. It once ranked among India's most valuable startups, sponsored the Indian cricket team and FIFA World Cup, and has since faced insolvency proceedings and unpaid debts. Very high consumer brand awareness in India, though financially distressed.

Online learning platform founded in 2012 by Stanford professors Andrew Ng and Daphne Koller, offering courses, professional certificates and online degrees from universities and companies, with Coursera for Business selling learning to employers and governments. Has well over 150 million registered learners and revenue near $700 million. Based in Mountain View, California, and listed on the NYSE (COUR) since March 2021. Total funding shown of about $470 million. Well-known consumer education brand worldwide.

Reckitt (Reckitt Benckiser) is a British consumer health and hygiene group, headquartered in Slough, behind brands such as Dettol, Lysol, Harpic, Durex, Nurofen, Strepsils, Gaviscon, Vanish, Finish and the Enfamil infant formula business (for sale from 2025). It sells to consumers through retailers in about 60 countries, with revenue over 14 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (RKT). Very high consumer visibility globally, and an experienced sports and event marketer.

wiki.title: Reckitt
wiki.text: Reckitt is a British multinational consumer goods company headquartered in Slough, United Kingdom. It manufactures health and hygiene products.

about: Prosus is an Amsterdam-based global consumer internet group, majority-controlled by Naspers, with major investments in Tencent, OLX classifieds, iFood, PayU, Swiggy, Delivery Hero and Just Eat Takeaway.com (acquired in 2025), serving hundreds of millions of users. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (PRX). Holding company, B2B itself, but its portfolio brands such as iFood and OLX are widely used consumer brands.

wiki.title: Prosus
wiki.text: Prosus N.V. is a Dutch investment group that invests and operates across sectors and markets with long-term growth potential. It is among the largest technology investors in the world.

about: B.TECH is an Egyptian consumer electronics and household appliance retailer, based in Cairo, selling TVs, phones, laptops, white goods and furniture through a large network of stores and online, with consumer financing. Founded in 2003, it has around 150 stores in Egypt and is expanding into Saudi Arabia, after an IPO on the Egyptian Exchange. Well-known consumer retail brand in Egypt, with funding of about $1.8 billion shown, which should be verified.

about: Magic Leap is a Plantation, Florida developer of augmented reality headsets, including the Magic Leap 2 headset for enterprise and healthcare, built with optics and waveguide technology. Customers are enterprises, hospitals and the military. Founded in 2010, it raised more than 4 billion dollars with backers such as Google and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, and pivoted from consumers to enterprise in 2020. Partnership with Google on AR was announced in 2024. Known in tech circles but with limited consumer sales.

wiki.title: Magic Leap
wiki.text: Magic Leap, Inc. is an American technology company that makes augmented reality headsets and software. Its first product was a head-mounted augmented reality display, called Magic Leap One, which superimposes 3D computer-generated imagery over real world objects. It is attempting to construct a light-field chip using silicon photonics. The company has since released the Magic Leap 2 and stopped selling the Magic Leap 1. Magic Leap was founded by Rony Abovitz in 2010 and has raised $2.6 billion from a list of investors including Google and Alibaba Group. Ross Rosenberg became CEO in 2023.

about: CyberArk is a Newton, Massachusetts-based identity security company, founded in Israel, whose privileged access management software protects credentials of administrators and machines. Listed on Nasdaq (CYBR), and agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Palo Alto Networks for about $25 billion. Customers are large enterprises and governments. Revenue is over $1 billion. B2B with strong recognition in cybersecurity.

wiki.title: CyberArk
wiki.text: CyberArk Software Ltd. is an Israeli information security company and a subsidiary of Palo Alto Networks offering identity management. The company's technology is utilized primarily in the financial services, energy, retail, healthcare, and government markets. CyberArk is headquartered in Petach-Tikva, with its United States headquarters located in Newton, MA. The company also has offices throughout the Americas, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Japan.

about: Vice Media was a New York-based digital media and broadcasting group known for Vice.com, Vice News, Vice TV and creative agency Virtue, which filed for bankruptcy in May 2023 and was bought by Fortress and lenders for about $350 million. Its funding history exceeded $1.6 billion. A recognised youth media brand but much diminished.

IM8 is a Charlotte, North Carolina nutritional supplements brand co-founded with David Beckham, offering science-backed daily nutrition products such as its Daily Ultimate Essentials drink mix. Launched in 2023, it is owned by Prenetics, the Nasdaq-listed health firm, and sold direct to consumers online and in some retail. Beckham is the brand's face and an investor. Rapidly growing consumer brand with a celebrity link, a natural fit for sports sponsorship.

TaskUs is a customer care and back-office outsourcing company, listed on Nasdaq (TASK) with a headquarters in New Braunfels, Texas. It provides content moderation, customer support and AI data services to digital companies such as Meta, Uber and Airbnb, through delivery centres in the Philippines, India and other countries. Revenue is about $1 billion. Controlled by Blackstone and founders. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: TaskUs
wiki.text: Task Us is an American multinational outsourcing company that handles content moderation, customer experience, artificial intelligence, operations and risk & response services for companies around the world, including Facebook and DoorDash.

about: Sonangol E.P. is Angola's state-owned national oil company, headquartered in Luanda. It holds concession rights over the country's oil and gas, manages exploration and production partnerships with international majors, and has downstream interests in refining, fuel distribution, shipping and trading, plus a banking and real estate legacy now being restructured. Revenue comes from crude sales and royalties. It is wholly owned by the Angolan state. Very well known in Angola, with a national sponsorship profile in sport and culture.

wiki.title: Sonangol Group
wiki.text: Group Sonangol (Portuguese: Grupo Sonangol) is a parastatal that formerly oversaw petroleum and natural gas production in Angola. The group consisted of Sonangol E.P. (Portuguese: Sociedade Nacional de Combustíveis de Angola, E.P.) and its many subsidiaries. The subsidiaries generally had Sonangol E.P. as a primary client, along with other corporate, commercial, and individual clients. In 2023, Sonangol produced 202,000 barrels of oil with an income of US$ 10.9 billion.

about: OpenAI is a San Francisco artificial intelligence company, founded in 2015, that develops large language and multimodal models and the ChatGPT consumer app, plus the API, Codex and Sora products, sold to developers, enterprises and hundreds of millions of weekly users. Revenue comes from subscriptions, API use and enterprise licences, in the billions of dollars. Microsoft is its largest investor, and the company has raised well over 100 billion dollars. Very high consumer brand awareness, among the most recognised technology names worldwide.

wiki.title: OpenAI
wiki.text: OpenAI Group PBC is an American artificial intelligence (AI) public benefit corporation (PBC) headquartered in San Francisco, California. It develops "frontier" generative AI models, particularly its generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) series of large language models. Its release of ChatGPT in November 2022 accelerated an AI boom, leading to widespread use of generative AI; as of September 2026, ChatGPT is the fifth-most-visited website globally. OpenAI also releases the GPT Image models and Codex, an AI coding agent. In March 2026, OpenAI closed a funding round with a post-money valuation of US$852 billion, making it one of the most val

about: Boldyn Networks is a London-based neutral host network infrastructure company, formerly BAI Communications, which builds and runs shared 5G, in-building and small cell wireless, WiFi and fibre networks for transport systems, stadiums, universities, venues and cities. Customers include mobile operators and transit agencies, such as the New York City Subway and the London Underground. Funding is about 1.2 billion dollars. B2B infrastructure brand with little consumer awareness, though its networks serve large venues and stadiums.

wiki.title: BAI Communications
wiki.text: BAI Communications, formerly Broadcast Australia, is an Australian telecommunications systems company.

about: Topeka, Kansas, financial services group focused on retirement, with annuity, life insurance and asset management businesses sold through independent advisers, banks and broker-dealers. Customers are individual savers and retirees; revenue comes from premiums, fees and investment spreads. Managing well over $100 billion of assets, and controlled since 2021 by Eldridge Industries, the investment group of Todd Boehly. Sponsors some US sports and community properties but has limited national consumer brand awareness; funding of $1.15 billion was shown for September 2025.

London-based business software firm, described by Crunchbase as a leading supplier of SAP Business One and related enterprise software, classified under business intelligence. Presumably sells ERP software, implementation and support to small and mid-sized businesses. The $1 billion funding figure shown looks unusual for a firm of this type and may be an OCR or data error. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: New York independent film and television studio and distributor behind award-winning titles such as Moonlight, Lady Bird, Hereditary, Midsommar, Uncut Gems and Everything Everywhere All at Once, as well as TV series like Euphoria with HBO. Founded in 2012, it earns money from theatrical releases, streaming deals, television production and branded merchandise and a growing consumer retail business. Valued at about $3.5 billion after a 2022 round led by Thrive Capital; total funding about $375 million. Very strong brand among young film and culture audiences.

Lifting Control Holding is an Italian manufacturer of loader cranes, based in Milan, Lombardy. The Crunchbase entry gives a funding figure of 535 million (currency not shown) with the latest event in September 2026, suggesting a private-equity-backed holding company. The input does not state its brands, customers, ownership or scale. Most likely a B2B industrial supplier to truck and construction equipment markets. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

The location was not captured, and the supplied description is incomplete. Several companies use this name, so the identity, products, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the input. It appears to be a recently funded AI company. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

wiki.title: Instinct
wiki.what: Behaviour due to innate biological factors
wiki.text: Instinct is the inherent inclination of a living organism towards a particular complex behaviour, containing innate (inborn) elements. The simplest example of an instinctive behaviour is a fixed action pattern (FAP), in which a very short to medium length sequence of actions, without variation, are carried out in response to a corresponding clearly defined stimulus. Every animal has instincts, including humans.

about: Serval is an AI-native IT service management startup that uses agents to automate help desk requests, access management and internal workflows, aiming to replace tools such as ServiceNow and Jira Service Management. The data tags it under agentic AI and records about $272M in funding in 2026. Customers are the IT teams of mid-sized and large companies. B2B software brand known among technology investors and IT leaders, with no consumer awareness. Details should be confirmed.

wiki.title: Serval
wiki.text: The serval is a wild small cat native to Africa. It is widespread in sub-Saharan countries, where it inhabits grasslands, wetlands, moorlands and bamboo thickets. Across its range, it occurs in protected areas, and hunting it is either prohibited or regulated in range countries.

about: Pershing Square Capital Management is a New York hedge fund and investment manager founded by Bill Ackman, known for concentrated positions in public companies such as Hilton, Chipotle, Restaurant Brands, Howard Hughes and Alphabet. It manages about US$15 billion, partly through the listed Pershing Square Holdings (London and Amsterdam), and has pursued a US listing of its vehicles. Funding of about $1.05B was recorded in 2024. Financial investor whose founder is a media figure, but with no consumer brand.

Space42 is an Abu Dhabi AI-powered space technology company formed in 2024 through the merger of Bayanat and Yahsat, listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (SPACE42). It operates satellite communications, earth observation and geospatial intelligence services, with government and defence customers in the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Funding of about $696M was recorded in 2025. Government-backed B2B technology company, with modest public awareness in the UAE.

Ubiquity is an Overland Park, Kansas company that invests in, develops and operates digital infrastructure, in particular data centres and related facilities, aiming to support cloud and AI computing demand. The Crunchbase entry records about $770M of funding in 2025. Public information on specific sites, owners and capacity is limited. It is a private B2B infrastructure firm with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: MaryRuth Organics is a Los Angeles dietary supplement brand known for liquid vitamins, multivitamins, collagen and wellness products for adults and children, sold online, at Target, Walmart, Amazon and in supermarkets. Founded by Mary Ruth Swift, it grew rapidly through social media and has received a major investment recorded at about $583M in 2025. Customers are health-conscious consumers, and it has been popular with influencers. Fast-growing consumer brand with strong social media presence and mainstream retail distribution.

about: Tawal is a Saudi telecom tower company that owns, builds and manages passive ICT infrastructure, with tens of thousands of towers across the Kingdom, serving mobile operators such as STC, Mobily and Zain. Based in Riyadh and linked to the Public Investment Fund. Ownership has changed through sale and investment deals, so check current shareholders. Funding of 1.42 billion dollars was recorded in August 2023. B2B infrastructure with little consumer awareness.

about: Persona is a San Francisco identity verification platform that helps businesses confirm user identities, prevent fraud and meet compliance with KYC and AML checks using IDs, selfies and database lookups. Customers include fintechs, marketplaces and large consumer apps. Founded in 2019, it has raised about 417 million dollars including a 2025 round at a valuation of about 2 billion dollars. B2B software with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Persona
wiki.text: A persona (plural personae or personas) is a strategic mask of identity in public, the public image of one's personality, the social role that one adopts, or simply a fictional character. It is also considered "an intermediary between the individual and the institution." Persona studies is an academic field developed by communication and media scholars. The related notions of "impression management" and "presentation of self" have been discussed by Erving Goffman in the 1950s.
